Outcome: Depressive symptoms (lower is better)

## Study A
Found: benefit
Claim: Higher 25OHD was associated with lower HDRS depression scores after treatment in all patients treated for depression.
Sentence: "We observed a negative correlation between the 25OHD and HDRS score after treatment in all patients treated for depression and in subgroups of women and subjects with recurrent depression."
Measured as: HDRS score after treatment
Population: 99 patients aged 46.9 ± 11 years treated for depression
Intervention: Not applicable (observational; serum 25OHD measured)
Comparator: None (correlation across participants)
Design: case-control study
Sample size: 144
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

## Study B
Found: harm
Claim: Patients with cognitive impairment had lower NPI dysphoria/depression scores (fewer symptoms) than cognitively normal patients.
Sentence: "On the NPI, the CI group had significantly lower scores (indicating fewer symptoms) than the CN group across all 12 domains, including delusions, hallucinations, agitation/aggression, dysphoria/depression, anxiety, elation/euphoria, apathy/indifference, disinhibition, irritability/lability, aberrant motor activity, nighttime behaviours/sleep disturbances, and appetite/eating disorders, as well as higher total NPI scores (p < 0.05)."
Measured as: NPI dysphoria/depression domain score
Population: Patients with ESRD undergoing maintenance haemodialysis
Intervention: Serum 25(OH)D level (measured, not given)
Comparator: Cognitively normal group vs cognitively impaired group
Design: case-control study
Sample size: 132
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported
